pl-l4d47c5-d1e115.summary: Asks whether, after the judgment, demons, whom Scripture calls executioners and torturers of souls, will preside in hell over the wicked to punish them.

pl-l4d47c5-d1e118.summary: Cites Paul: Christ will then abolish every principality, power, and virtue; while the world lasts, angels preside over angels, demons over demons, men over men, but when all are gathered, all prelacy will cease.
claims: All prelacy ceases after the judgment.

pl-l4d47c5-d1e127.summary: Reports some who think that after the judgment demons will not have power to torment men as now, but as demons are tormented by God's power without creaturely ministry, so the reprobate will be subjected to eternal torments by divine power alone, not by demons' working.
claims: Some hold God alone torments the damned.

pl-l4d47c5-d1e131.summary: Notes that the authority does not compel this, since though it says demons will not preside over demons nor men over men, it does not decide whether demons preside over men to torment them.
claims: The text leaves the question open.

pl-l4d47c5-d1e134.summary: Reports some who think demons will be men's torturers in punishment as they were their tempters in fault.
claims: Some hold demons torment those they tempted.

pl-l4d47c5.summary: Asks whether after the judgment demons will preside over the damned in hell as torturers. Paul says Christ will then abolish every principality and power, so all prelacy ceases; hence some think demons will not torment men, both being tormented by God's power alone. But that text does not decide whether demons preside over men for torment, so some think they will be torturers in punishment as they were tempters in fault.
claims: All prelacy ceases after the judgment.
Whether demons torment the damned is disputed.
Some hold demons will torment those they tempted.
